nodes.label: desktop.elf Userland DE Server
nodes.rationale: Goal: move the GUI out of kernel space into a userland desktop.elf process that owns the framebuffer via mmap, manages windows, and runs as a fork+exec from init, so GUI code no longer lives in kernel space.

nodes.label: Unified Input Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Mouse/keyboard events flow through a single kernel ring buffer (kernel/input.c) with input_event_t entries; the desktop renders the cursor at a fixed <=100Hz frame rate independent of PS/2 event bursts to keep movement smooth under high injection rates.

nodes.label: Shared-Memory Window Buffers
nodes.rationale: Apps write pixels directly to their shared-memory window buffer and the compositor reads it without any memcpy, avoiding per-frame buffer copies between app and DE.

nodes.label: Performance Targets (60fps, <200ms app launch)
nodes.rationale: Compositor aims for 60fps (16ms frame budget), <5s boot to desktop in QEMU, <200ms app launch, ~3MB per window buffer, 32 max windows, and >70% of frames partial-update via dirty rects; optimizations include dirty-rect tracking, LRU glyph cache, shared-memory buffers, kernel-side blit, and batched socket sends.

nodes.label: Thin CMake Wrapper Over Makefile
nodes.rationale: CMake provides a thin wrapper so developers can run `cmake .` then `make`/`make run` without modifying the original Makefile-based build system.
